transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Sable Head of Platform), Luca Fernandez (SRE), Amir O'Neill (CTO)

Summary:
Short: Postmortem follow-up after 2026-11-08 incident where a model rollout + KV cache interaction caused sustained latency/500s for Sable Labs traffic. We reviewed root cause, temporary mitigations (rollback + rate-limit throttles), long-term fixes (canary gating, improved autoscaling policies, stronger tracing), and agreed on ownerable action items.

Topics:
- Root cause: cache eviction/serialization bug + aggressive canary rollout settings + insufficient autoscale headroom
- Immediate mitigation: rollback to prior model + emergency throttle rule + manual patch to cache serialization
- Reliability improvements: CI canary tests, autoscaling policy tuning, observability (span traces, token-level latency), runbooks and on-call playbooks
- Security/regulatory: confirm no customer data persisted in logs, KMS checks

Action Items (verbalized during call):
- Ravi to push hotfix and run staging soak (24h)
- Jordan to share runbook and rollback doc + security artifact link
- Priya to provide request traces and traffic profiles
- Maya to follow up on pricing credits and remediation SLAs

Transcript body (imperfect automated transcription, timestamps approximate):
00:00 Speaker 1: hey everyone thanks for joining um we'll kick off, this is Maya from Redwood
00:12 Maya Chen (AE): Hi all, thanks. The goal for today is to align on the postmortem and make sure the action items are clear. Ravi will run through the technical findings.
00:32 Ravi Patel (SE): OK so quick recap, on 2026-11-08 we rolled model v2.1 to 60% traffic across the dedicated pool and shortly after we saw latencies go from 80ms to multi-second p95 and a bump in 500s. At first we thought it was GPU memory, but traces pointed at the KV cache layer causing long serialization stalls.
01:05 Luca (SRE): yeah the errors looked like timeouts trying to read from the K V cash, it serialized a lot more than expected, and our client retries amplified the issue.
01:28 Amir (CTO): can you clarify why it hit only our production cluster? we run similar load in preprod.
01:40 Ravi: a few contributing factors — first the canary gating was misconfigured, it allowed a bigger traffic ramp than intended; second our autoscaler policy had conservative headroom thresholds so we didn't auto scale quickly; third the cache serialization change in model code introduced a blocking path under hot get access patterns.
02:05 Priya: and were there any data residency or logs that include PII? that's a big concern for legal.
02:18 Jordan (CSM): quick answer — we've audited the logs for the window and there's no customer PII; we used truncated identifiers and KMS-encrypted artifacts. We'll share the security audit doc after this call.
03:02 Ravi: immediate remediation path we took: rolled back to v2.0, added temporary rate-limiting on the route to reduce retry storms, and applied a small patch to the cache serialization to avoid blocking the event loop. That got p95 back to baseline in ~20 minutes.
03:40 Luca: thanks, that rollback helped but the transient 10-15 minute window caused several downstream jobs to fail, which is the main customer impact.
04:05 Maya: right and Sable lost throughput on search and a batch notification worker — we want to avoid that pain in future.
05:12 Ravi: for longer-term fixes we propose: automated canary gating (both traffic % and latency guardrails), improved autoscale headroom on Dedicated pools, and stronger KV cache regression tests that emulate the shard hot-gets pattern.
06:00 Amir: about the autoscale headroom, can we set burst capacity or pre-warm nodes? we can't accept slow recovery windows.
06:20 Ravi: yes we can — Redwood Dedicated supports configurable burst capacity; we'll propose a config that keeps X% spare GPU capacity for critical routes or a scheduled pre-warm during known peaks. We'll share the config suggestion.
07:00 Priya: any change to encryption or logging? we need explicit confirmation that logs saved during the incident are encrypted and stored per our contract.
07:18 Jordan: confirmed — logs from the incident window are KMS encrypted and retained per the agreed policy. I'll attach the retention and KMS key IDs in the post-call doc.
08:05 Maya: let's talk about observability — what traces did you get and what do you need from Sable?
08:20 Ravi: we have partial distributed traces but some spans were missing due to sampling and client-side short timeouts. It would help if Sable can share the client request IDs and the traffic profile for the hour around the incident. That will let us replay and reproduce in staging.
09:00 Priya: we'll extract anonymized request ids and traffic profile, we have to scrub user ids per policy. We'll aim to share by eod 2026-11-14.
10:30 Amir: on the followup timeline, what are realistic ETA for the hotfix and for a canary gating change?
10:42 Ravi: hotfix into staging within 24h and 24h soak. Canary gating config change and additional regression tests within two weeks; autoscale config proposal in 3 business days.
12:00 Maya: ok let's be explicit on owners and dates — I'll capture that in the notes and Jordan will distribute.

(roughly 20 minutes of discussion omitted here for brevity but covered on the call: deep dive into serialization codepath, sample traces, canary configuration schema, suggested autoscale thresholds, proposed rollback playbook)

32:05 Ravi: one more technical note — the serialization fallback we added is a non-blocking path that uses pre-allocated buffers; it avoids allocation storms that we saw. We'll include the diff in the repo link.
33:10 Luca: curious if this was triggered by particular request patterns (e.g., long context or heavy beam search)?
33:28 Ravi: we saw higher token counts on a subset of requests during the traffic spike and a small change in model output handling increased CPU work on the CPU side which amplified serialization delays.
35:00 Priya: are there recommendations for request shaping on our side? like limiting max tokens or adaptive batching?
35:18 Ravi: short term we recommend request shaping and adaptive client-side retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Long term, Redwood Optimize has suggestions for batching but we'll surface a custom config for Sable.
38:50 Amir: any regulatory signoffs we need to get after the fix? SOC2 audit artifacts?
39:10 Jordan: no new SOC2 artifacts triggered, but we'll attach the incident timeline and audit results for your compliance team.
41:00 Maya: recap of next steps and owners — Ravi pushes hotfix to staging and notifies when soak is green; Jordan sends runbook and security doc; Priya shares traces; Maya to follow-up on credits and SLA impacts.
41:25 Priya: we'll also run a reproducible load in preprod and share results by 2026-11-17.
42:05 Amir: once hotfix verified, let's schedule a gated canary with Redwood SE to validate at low traffic.
42:20 Ravi: yes we'll schedule a canary run on 2026-11-15 and monitor p50/p95/p99 and 500 rates.
50:00 Maya: any blockers preventing action items?
50:12 Priya: none from our side — we just need the traces and the playbook.
50:30 Jordan: I'll get the playbook over by tomorrow.
56:10 Maya: thanks everyone for moving fast; we'll reconvene after the staging soak or in 5 business days.
56:25 Amir: thanks all.
56:30 Meeting ended.
